method: Crypto cycle phase: accumulation (MVRV ≤ 1), distribution (MVRV in the top 10% of its last 4 years), else bull (price above its 200-day average) or bear. Coins without on-chain data use Bitcoin's phase. Long-term phase scores: accumulation 8.5, bull 6, bear 3.5, distribution 3.5; timing: 6.5, 6, 4, 5.

accumulation.label: Accumulation
accumulation.note: Price is below the average cost of all coins (MVRV ≤ 1): holders are at a loss on average. In 2012–2026 Bitcoin was higher one year later in 98–100% of such days (median +93%); Ethereum in 70–96%. Bottoms form here, but it can last months.

bull.label: Bull market
bull.note: Price above its 200-day average with holders in profit but not euphoric: the trend phase of the cycle.

bear.label: Bear market
bear.note: Price below its 200-day average while holders are still in profit on average (MVRV > 1): historically weak — Bitcoin's median one-year return from such days was −9%, Ethereum's −26%. The cycle usually ends with a drop into accumulation (price under the average cost).

distribution.label: Distribution
distribution.note: MVRV in the top 10% of its last 4 years: holders sit on large profits and long-term holders sell into strength. Momentum can carry prices higher for weeks, but one-year returns from here have been poor since 2019.

near.phase_source: Bitcoin's cycle (no on-chain data for this coin)
